query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Use GitHub to inspect accessible repositories and branches, fetch repository files, update multiple repository files, create a public static preview repository, enable GitHub Pages, and commit generated content/configuration files.
query_ground_truth.query: create public repository and enable GitHub Pages
query_ground_truth.intent: Create a new public static preview repository and enable GitHub Pages on it.

requirement_groups.purpose: enable GitHub Pages and commit content/configuration files

request.query: create public repository and enable GitHub Pages

results.use_case: create public repository and enable GitHub Pages
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if target repository is unknown or avoiding overwrite)] [Prerequisite]: Discover/confirm the repository using GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY (or scan via GITHUB_LIST_REPOSITORIES_FOR_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER; treat not-found as create-needed).
[Required (public impact)] [Step]: Get confirmation, then create the repository using GITHUB_CREATE_A_REPOSITORY_FOR_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER (set visibility/settings appropriate for publishing).
[Required] [Step]: Add site entry content and assets using GITHUB_COMMIT_MULTIPLE_FILES (commit to the intended publishing branch; create the branch on first commit if needed).
[Fallback (if bulk commit is unsuitable or a small update fails)] [Fallback]: Create/update a single file using GITHUB_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FILE_CONTENTS (provide latest sha when updating).
[Optional (if validating publish source before enabling)] [Prerequisite]: Confirm the publishing branch/path contains the entry file using GITHUB_GET_A_TREE.
[Required] [Next Step]: Enable/configure static hosting using GITHUB_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_GITHUB_PAGES_SITE (set source_branch and a valid source_path).
[Optional (if a build identifier is available and readiness is required)] [Next Step]: Check the build status using GITHUB_GET_GITHUB_PAGES_BUILD.
known_pitfalls: [GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY] 404 Not Found can mean the repository does not exist or is not accessible; confirm before treating as fatal.
[GITHUB_CREATE_A_REPOSITORY_FOR_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER] HTTP 422 can occur if the repository name already exists for the account; recover by fetching and continuing with commits/config.
[GITHUB_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_GITHUB_PAGES_SITE] source_path must be exactly "/" or "/docs"; other values may return "Invalid request data provided".

[GITHUB_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_GITHUB_PAGES_SITE] The response may include an html_url while status is null right after enablement; HTTPS enforcement may 404 until a certificate exists—retry later or omit enforcement initially.
[GITHUB_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FILE_CONTENTS] 409 conflict occurs when updating with a stale sha; refetch the latest sha before retrying.

toolkit_connection_statuses.description: GitHub is a code hosting platform for version control and collaboration, offering Git-based repository management, issue tracking, and continuous integration features
toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=github. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="github") to create a connection BEFORE executing any github tools.

GITHUB_CREATE_A_REPOSITORY_FOR_THE_AUTHE.description: Creates a new repository for the authenticated user, optionally within an organization if `team_id` is specified.

name.description: The name of the repository. Must be unique within your account. Will be used in the repository URL (github.com/username/repo-name). Can only contain alphanumeric characters, hyphens, underscores, and periods.

private.description: Whether the repository is private (true) or public (false).

team_id.description: The ID of the team to be granted access. Only valid if creating in an organization.

homepage.description: A URL with more information about the repository.

auto_init.description: Whether to initialize the repository with a README.

examples: This is a project about X.
description.description: A short description of the repository.

is_template.description: Whether this repository is a template repository.

has_downloads.description: Whether downloads are enabled (deprecated by GitHub and may not be configurable).

allow_auto_merge.description: Whether to allow auto-merge on pull requests.

license_template.description: SPDX license key identifier (lowercase). Examples: 'mit', 'apache-2.0', 'gpl-3.0'. Must be one of the GitHub-supported licenses.

allow_merge_commit.description: Whether to allow merging pull requests with a merge commit.

allow_rebase_merge.description: Whether to allow rebase-merging pull requests.

allow_squash_merge.description: Whether to allow squash-merging pull requests.

merge_commit_title.description: The default title for a merge commit. `PR_TITLE` uses the pull request's title. `MERGE_MESSAGE` uses a classic title like 'Merge pull request #123 from branch-name'. Required when `merge_commit_message` is set. Valid combinations: (PR_TITLE, PR_BODY), (PR_TITLE, BLANK), (MERGE_MESSAGE, PR_TITLE).

merge_commit_message.description: The default message for a merge commit. `PR_BODY` uses the pull request's body. `PR_TITLE` uses the pull request's title. `BLANK` results in a blank commit message. Valid combinations with merge_commit_title: (PR_TITLE, PR_BODY), (PR_TITLE, BLANK), (MERGE_MESSAGE, PR_TITLE).

delete_branch_on_merge.description: Whether to automatically delete head branches when pull requests are merged.

squash_merge_commit_title.description: The default title for a squash merge commit. `PR_TITLE` uses the pull request's title. `COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE` uses the commit's title (if only one commit) or the pull request's title (if multiple commits).

squash_merge_commit_message.description: The default message for a squash merge commit. `PR_BODY` uses the pull request's body. `COMMIT_MESSAGES` uses the branch's commit messages. `BLANK` results in a blank commit message.

GITHUB_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_GITHUB_PAGES_SIT.description: Tool to enable or update GitHub Pages configuration for a repository. Use when setting up GitHub Pages for static site deployment or modifying Pages settings like custom domains and HTTPS enforcement.

repo.description: The name of the repository without the .git extension. Not case-sensitive.

cname.description: Custom domain for the Pages site (e.g., 'example.com'). Set to null to remove custom domain. Only used during updates.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization). Not case-sensitive.

build_type.description: Build process type: 'legacy' for traditional GitHub Pages build from a branch, 'workflow' for GitHub Actions. When 'workflow', source_branch and source_path are ignored.

source_path.description: The directory path within source_branch containing the site files: '/' for root or '/docs' for docs folder. Ignored if build_type is 'workflow'.

source_branch.description: The repository branch to use for GitHub Pages source (e.g., 'main', 'gh-pages'). Required if build_type is 'legacy'. Ignored if build_type is 'workflow'.

https_enforced.description: Whether to enforce HTTPS for the Pages site. Only used during updates.

GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY.description: Retrieves detailed information about an existing and accessible GitHub repository.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is case-insensitive.

owner.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is case-insensitive.
